main_text.head: NOBILISSIMO AMPLISSIMOQVE viro, D. Iohanni à Wattenuill florentissimæ Bernatum Reipubl. consuli dignissimo

p.i: PhilosophiaCic.Tus-cul.§. vitæ ducem, virtutis & veritatis indagatricem veteres esse dixerunt: cuius ope atque ductu homines principio congregati fuerint, & in vitæ societatem convocati. Cùm autem Philosophia potissimum in naturæ contemplatione, & in formandis moribus versetur: ac propterea præstantissimum hoc elogium Philosophiæ hisce duabus ipsius

page.notes: The large initial P is a woodcut, read as the first letter of "Philosophia"; the first line reads "Hilosophia" after it. The marginal note "Cic.Tus-cul.§." is partly worn: the hyphen after "Tu" and the "§" are uncertain, so the reading is approximate. The "viro" in the title is partly obscured by a mark over the "o", so it is uncertain. The small bullet at the left margin beside "florentissimæ" and the marks "* z" under the last line are printer's or scan marks, not text. "hisce" is followed by a stroke at the line end that may be an abbreviation sign; the text is left as "hisce". The paragraph continues on the next page.
